title: Vetala Extended Tale 91: The Hunter and the Wounded Swan

full_text:
Vikram retrieved the Vetala once more. The ghost spoke:

"A prince shot a white swan flying over the royal orchards. The wounded bird fell into the garden of a gentle youth, who gently lifted it, pulled out the cruel arrow, cleansed the wound with wild lotus oil, and nursed the bird back to health.

The hunter arrived, demanding the bird: 'I shot it with my arrow; it is my rightful prey by the law of the chase!' The gentle youth refused, saying: 'I saved its life; it belongs to me.'

They brought their dispute before the royal court of dharma.

Tell me, Vikram: by eternal natural law, to whom does the living swan belong?"

King Vikramaditya answered: "The living swan belongs wholly to the one who saved its life. The hunter sought only to end its existence for sport, while the healer gave it life through compassion. He who preserves life has an absolute and eternal claim over him who seeks to destroy it. Compassion is the supreme law."

"Rightly judged, O Vikram!" laughed the Vetala, flying back into the branches.
moral: The right to life belongs to the one who protects and saves, never to the one who seeks to destroy.
